Pte. A.W. Oldag.
COPY.
26, Willow Road, Hampstead, N.W.3.
23rd February 1946.

Dear Old Jo,

I very much hope by the time you get this letter you will have had a visit from Marie Louise; she was going to try and get up to see you. In case you haven't I'll tell you the good news - that I had a special release last week! It's a real triumph for the Defence Committee and I'm so pleased for Juge's sake for them to have a real success at last. She has worked terrible hard and really efficiently for a long time and to have something concrete at last is very encouraging for her. But you can imagine how I felt when I was just sitting down waiting for the orderly to bring around the cup of cocoa and instead he came up and told me to pack up my kit as I had a special! I couldn't believe it! It was on the Monday and I was due to go up for an appeal Tribunal the following Friday and was thinking that the earliest possible would have been two or three days after that. So it came out of the blue and I just went up like a rocket! I had been feeling a bit low, too, as I'd had a doze of gastric flu for the week previous, but I never felt better than when I got outside those gates!

But, dear old Jo, I feel almost guilty telling you all this while you are still penned up - but I have a feeling that it won't be for much longer. Won't it be wonderful when we can all be together again and you can live freely and in the open with no more hole-in-corner secrecy! How we shall celebrate your release! M.L. told me of your decision regarding the bottle of rum and we shall have to try hard to obtain it for you. If only we knew when!

As you see from my address I am at the moment staying with John and Peter again, not to mention their family. Young Charlotte is a dumpling who shuffles along on her bottom at an alarming rate and young Judith is looking over my shoulder at this moment. She sends her love to you, altho' she's never seen you, but if you're a friend of mine you're a friend of hers. Needless to say J.&.P. send their warmest greetings to you and John includes his abject apologies and promises to write SOON. The enclosed photograph is one of a series taken in accordance with a decision made at the Glasgow Conference where the Glasgow Comrades thought it would be a good thing if we "back room boys(& Girls)" had our photo's printed in the paper to prove to our readers that we are real (& more or less ordinary) people and not sinister figures in the background. So far only myself and John have had our photo's taken and they have not appeared in the paper. We are all so bashful you know!

I have heard from Ivor and intend writing to him soon. It's a bad business about his leg. Have you had any more letters from Bill??? Our other friends Bill and Eric have not been seen since the balloon went up - my god, nearly 18 months ago now! What a miserable year we've had of it - altho' I do admire the way you have kept your spirits up, obviously intending to get as much out of it as possible. V. has just arrived. We are going for a walk on the Heath. He's heard from M.L. and she's off to see you to-day (Sunday) Am so pleased. Hope to get up to see you myself sometime. Love from J.P.V., and all the Comrades.

Tom E. / not forgetting Philips

Certified true copy and typed by me -
Welfare Officer,
No. 10 Military Detention Barrack.
